newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk army seeks investigation of Islamist channel.
newsitem.headline: Turk army seeks investigation of Islamist channel.

text.p: Turkey's secularist military has asked the country's television watchdog to investigate an Islamist television channel for a news report allegedly insulting the army, a board official said on Friday.
"The military second in command has complained about a news report broadcast by Channel 7 in May," the senior official of the Turkey's Board of Radio and Television (RTUK) told Reuters.
"The report was on a speech by the chairman of MUSIAD -- an association of Moslem businessmen -- We are looking into it," he said. Details of the report were not available.
The army demanded RTUK close down the channel, saying it had insulted the army, the Yeni Yuzyil daily said on Wednesday.
The official said the board, which has the power to shut down television channels only temporarily, would make a decision over the Channel 7 row next week.

Turkey's powerful military authorities are locked in a protracted dispute with the Islamist-led government of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan over growing religious activism which the army sees as a threat to the country's officially secular system.
The army in February issued a list of its demands designed to clamp down on growing Islamic fervour, but Erbakan has so far resisted their implementation.
Erbakan has called for early elections in an effort to head off the deadlock. But his government now lacks a majority in parliament which would need to approve the move.
